we propose a strategy to fit heterogeneous latent class models to rating scores data, that the strategy can be used to identify latent groups of consumers with similar response patterns and to characterize them in terms of covariates, that the strategy is illustrated by analyzing a real data set, that the strategy has a number of limitations, that the strategy should be used with caution, and that the strategy can provide useful information for marketing purposes.

- the analysis of data from rating scales, - the use of latent class models to identify groups of consumers and characterize them, - the inclusion of covariates to explain the heterogeneity of consumers and to identify potential predictors of the preferences of consumers, - the implementation of the strategy in the covLCA package.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a heterogeneous model with covariates on the probabilities of latent class membership is preferred.
the covariate analysis in LCMs is not a simple extension of the standard LCM, but it requires a more complex and careful approach, which we propose here.
the latent class models with covariates can be successfully used to analyze rating scores.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed strategy allows us to identify the most important factors that influence the preferences of Belgian consumers for supermarkets and to characterize the different types of consumer.
the proposed strategy is a powerful tool to analyze rating data and discover the preferences of consumers, which can be applied in many marketing contexts.

the proposed strategy allows to obtain a good understanding of the structure of the data, the latent classes of the model and the covariates that are related to the preferences and the behavior of the consumers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a model with covariates should not be preferred to the basic model if it is only marginally better and it does not provide a better interpretation.
the inclusion of covariates can lead to more parsimonious and interpretable models, and that the strategy we propose can help in identifying the most relevant covariates.
the inclusion of covariates in latent class models can lead to an improved understanding of the data and to more realistic conclusions.
